comparison: Perfect agreement on urea ChIP-seq method validation (C47-C65). Both evaluations strongly support the methodological innovation, with peer reviewers explicitly praising it as 'new and innovative' and confirming the technical validity of the urea treatment approach.

Strong agreement on mutual exclusivity of SATB1 and CTCF binding (C66-C78, with C68 only in OpenEval). Both evaluations accept the quantitative evidence and statistical support. Peer reviewers state the authors 'convincingly make the case' and findings are 'supported by a wealth of controls.'

Agreement on validation controls showing urea ChIP-seq works for other proteins (C79-C85, with C81-C82 only in OpenEval). Peer reviewers explicitly validated that 'urea-ChIP and standard ChIP yield similar profiles for CTCF and polycomb complex subunits,' confirming method specificity.

Complete agreement on independence of SATB1 and CTCF binding (C86-C93). Both evaluations accept the genome-wide ChIP-seq comparisons and biochemical co-binding analysis as strong evidence for distinct roles in chromatin organization.

Perfect agreement on Hi-C analysis showing SATB1 independence from TAD organization (C94-C99). Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed that 'knock down of SATB1 does not affect the TAD patterns,' treating this as a key validated finding.

Strong agreement on SATB1-KO validation (C100-C105), though peer review also includes C106, C114-C115 related to functional loci. Both evaluations strongly validate the KO controls, with peer reviewers noting 'SATB1 KO cells provide a nice control for the specificity of signals.'

Partial overlap on functional loci analysis. OpenEval R7 focuses on specific loci with SATB1-dependent regulation (C106-C115), while peer R6 includes only C106, C114-C115 alongside KO validation. Both support the two-tiered binding model at functional loci.

Partial overlap on functional context. OpenEval R7 emphasizes functional loci evidence (C106-C115), while peer R15 treats C107-C113 as supporting contextual details rather than primary findings. Both accept the biological relevance but with different emphasis.

Strong agreement on urea 4C-seq and long-range interactions (C116-C128, with C123-C125 only in OpenEval). Peer reviewers endorsed that 'SATB1 controls long-range interactions' and findings demonstrate 'functionally significant layers of chromatin organization.'

Partial overlap on gene expression correlation. OpenEval R8 includes comprehensive 4C-seq analysis (C116-C128), while peer R8 focuses specifically on gene expression correlation aspects (C6, C7, C53, C54, C123-C125). Both accept functional significance.

Strong agreement on cell-type-specific BUR occupancy (C129-C137, with C10, C52 only in peer review). Both evaluations accept the >10-fold variation and hierarchical pattern. Peer reviewers note 'cell type-specific differences' suggest functional relevance.

Strong agreement on BUR-LAD overlap (C8, C51, C139-C143, with C140-C143 emphasized). Both evaluations accept BURs as important sequence components of LADs. Peer reviewers acknowledge authors 'gain many binding events in silent regions represented by LADs.'

Perfect agreement on BURs outside LADs (C9, C145-C148). Both evaluations accept that BURs exclude enhancer peaks regardless of genomic context and reside in locally inaccessible chromatin. Peer reviewers note 'BURs are found enriched in LADs, but are also present in active chromatin.'

Agreement on overall two-tiered model (C3, C12, C55, C149-C150 in OpenEval; C12, C149-C150 in peer). Both endorse the model while peer reviewers acknowledge complexity, noting 'some readers may be left confused' and mechanistic details remain 'unclear.'

Partial overlap on model integration. OpenEval R12 presents comprehensive model (C3, C12, C55, C149-C150), while peer R7 emphasizes the two-tiered organization discovery (C3, C50, C55 plus 4C-seq claims). Both strongly support the model.

Partial agreement on BUR biochemical properties (C28-C34). OpenEval R13 focuses on BUR properties, while peer R13 includes broader SATB1 background (C1, C28-C44, C56-C57). Both treat these as established background supporting current findings.

Partial agreement on SATB1 background. OpenEval R14 covers SATB1 expression/function (C35-C41), while peer R13 includes this within comprehensive background (C1, C28-C44, C56-C57). Both accept as established context.

Partial agreement on study motivation. OpenEval R15 addresses limitations of standard ChIP-seq (C42-C46), while peer R13 includes this within broader background. Both accept these as establishing the problem the study addresses.

Partial agreement on foundational prior work. OpenEval R16 focuses on Cai et al. 2003 findings (C1, C56-C57), while peer R13 includes this within comprehensive background. Both treat as established conceptual foundation.

Strong agreement on chromatin organization background (C13-C27 in OpenEval; C13-C27, C45-C46 in peer). Both evaluations accept these as established background knowledge contextualizing SATB1's distinct role. No challenges from reviewers.

Agreement on SATB1 expression context (C138). OpenEval R18 treats this as supporting quantitative context, while peer R15 includes it among supporting contextual details. Both accept as adequately supported background information.
